patterns: Price before the block, every call: 15/15 sales calls had a number before any full beat block. Only 3 calls landed even one beat first, and 0 landed all five, so the 85 ceiling was in force on every call. Typical: "So is your property under an acre? ... So you have two options ... One is a quick fix." (Mathes 9/17). The order-card deferral line was never used.

Quick Fix first, TMCP never first with a recommendation (0/15). Even so, the one-quote rule held (0 offers to send both), and TMCP won 8 of 11 Mo-attributed quotes in these three days (Mathes, Campbell, Chen, Horvath, Hendrickson, Wilcox, Penrod, Harrod). Most of those callers picked it themselves. The three quick fixes (Kupietz, Willis, Gilbert) were callers Mo let choose or nudged ("Do you want to go with one time? You know, the five weeks"), including a 20-year infestation.

Capture and speed are strong: full capture with read-back on 10 of 14 completed sales calls; every promised quote was in Jobber within 1-6 minutes, with the correct plan and deposit (QF $150 / TMCP $0). The exceptions: a misspelled name delayed Mathes a day, and two calls (Emily, McCurdy) ended with almost nothing captured.

Accuracy leaks are new-claim and tier errors, not price-sheet errors: wrong acreage tier twice (Wilcox 1.5 ac, Penrod 3 ac at $100), unsubstantiated claims 3 times ("99% success ratio", "only ones who does moles in Washington", "10 years"), and invented or ignored coverage 3 times (Lake Stevens, Lynnwood, Centralia). Guarantee hit on 13 of 15.

Service calls: Mo describes TMCP as a scheduled taper ("weekly ... then semi weekly ... then monthly") on 3 calls (Wilcox, Peck, McMillin). That contradicts the any-activity-means-weekly rule and produced the week's only D grades (Kelsey Peck, twice).
